sc: Boy 4 years, puffy eyes, proteinuria 4+, albumin 15, normal BP, C3 and creatinine → Minimal change: steroids, no biopsy
Still proteinuric after 6 weeks of steroids → Steroid-resistant: biopsy (FSGS)
Nephrotic child on steroids with fever, abdominal pain, tender ascites → Pneumococcal peritonitis: IV ceftriaxone
f: Heavy proteinuria (≥ 3+, UPCR > 200 mg/mmol) + albumin < 25 g/L + oedema (± high cholesterol)
Periorbital then generalised oedema, ascites · normal BP, no haematuria (minimal change) · peak age 2–6 yr
Urine dipstick and UPCR · albumin, cholesterol · creatinine · C3 · HBsAg, HIV · biopsy only if atypical or resistant
Prednisolone 60 mg/m²/day × 4–6 wk, then 40 mg/m² alternate days × 4–6 wk · salt restriction · albumin 20% 0.5–1 g/kg only if hypovolaemic
Remission: dipstick negative 3 days · ~90% steroid-sensitive · frequent relapses: levamisole · resistant → biopsy
Infection (peritonitis) · thrombosis (cerebral venous) · hypovolaemia (abdominal pain, cold hands, high Hct) · steroid side effects
trap: Haematuria, hypertension or low C3 = not minimal change: biopsy · nephrotic in a 3-month-old = congenital · oedema with low albumin but no proteinuria = kwashiorkor or gut loss
